 Print Pankaj Tripathi says, 'I will put forward the concerns of filmmakers' on his role as a CBFC member and backs scrapping of Tatkal certification: 'You cannot expect the certification process to be completed in five hours' Pankaj Tripathi , who joined the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) as a member two months ago, has spoken about the board's new rules that have created a stir in the film industry . He says the aim is to make certification smoother and bring filmmakers closer to the board. What has changed at CBFC
 Since Pankaj Tripathi came on board, the CBFC has brought in a few notable guidelines. Producers must now submit the full, finished version of their film, and a title will not be treated as final until the certificate is issued. The board can also ask for changes to it. Pankaj Tripathi on bridging the gap
 After attending a recent meeting, the actor said the board wants to be closer to creators. He told MidDay, “I came to know that the CBFC wants to reduce the gap between filmmakers and itself. Intelligent filmmakers know how to make movies, keeping in mind the country they cater to, and the board wants to understand the filmmakers. As a member, I’m still learning about how things work. Whenever I am called for a meeting, I will put forward the concerns of filmmakers. Join conversation

 The CBFC has often landed in disputes over the years. Pankaj Tripathi stated that he feels the massive reach of cinema is the reason such issues grow so quickly. He said, “Films are a popular medium in India. Everything gets discussed and dissected quickly. Several people [on the board] watch the film. If there is a problem, it is to be discussed further. As artistes and filmmakers, we have to be mindful [of what we’re clearing], and to do so, diverse groups of people need to watch a film and [voice] their view at the certification level. ” Support for ending Tatkal certification 
 For the same reason, he supports the withdrawal of the Tatkal certification facility, which had come into force in June 2026. According to him, a decision this important needs careful examination at several levels. Pankaj Tripathi asserted, “The process of making a film takes months. You cannot expect the certification process to be completed in five hours. The members have responsibilities; they have to look at the objectives and guidelines. ” When the CBFC was reconstituted
 The new 18-member body is chaired by Shashi Shekhar Vempati. Its members include Suniel Shetty , Preity Zinta , Priyadarshan, Prosenjit and Ricky Kej , among others.
